dedupe_keys.name: economic census every five years including utilities transportation and warehousing sectors

description: The Economic Census is the U.S. Census Bureau's official five-year measure of American business, collected for years ending in 2 and 7 under a legal reporting requirement (Title 13). It covers establishments in most industries in the United States and the Island Areas, representing over eight million business locations, and tabulates by NAICS industry the number of establishments, employees, payroll and output (sales, value of shipments or revenue), with Geographic Area Statistics by state, metropolitan area, county and place, Establishment and Firm Size statistics and product lines (NAPCS). Infrastructure-relevant subject series include, for the utilities sector (NAICS 22), cost of purchased electricity and natural gas for resale and exported energy to Canada and Mexico; for transportation and warehousing, revenue-generating equipment and end-of-year inventories; and for construction, value of construction work by location and kind of business. Coverage: 2022 results released on a flow basis by industry; formatted tables for 2012, 2017 and 2022 on data.census.gov, FTP files for 2002 and 2007, and printed publications before 2002. Access: data.census.gov tables (xls, csv, zip), the FTP directory and the Census Data API (ecn groups, free key); free, public domain. Caveats: figures are suppressed where they would disclose a business, and a note says the Bureau is re-evaluating noise infusion; five-year gaps limit timeliness. Simulation uses: economic exposure of business activity by industry and area, utility sector revenue and cost structure, input-output and business interruption loss models. Related records: County Business Patterns, the petroleum bulk storage capacity tables of the same census, the Commodity Flow Survey and the NBER-CES manufacturing database.
